name: Optimistic PR review comments
description: Post PR review comments and replies optimistically so they appear the instant you hit submit, then reconcile to the server comment in the background. If the GitHub call fails, the placeholder is rolled back and the composer reopens with your draft intact.
commitTitle: feat: post PR review comments optimistically

steps.title: Mark placeholder comments in the data model
steps.body: Add an `optimistic` flag to `PRReviewComment`. A placeholder carries a temporary negative `id`, no `url`/`threadId`, and cannot yet be edited, deleted, or resolved, so downstream code can tell it apart from a real server comment.

callouts.body: The one field the rest of the change keys off. Negative ids never collide with GitHub ids, so we can find the exact placeholder to reconcile or roll back.

steps.title: Optimistic submit, reconcile, and rollback
steps.body: `makeOptimisticPRComment` builds the placeholder from the viewer's account. `submitComposer` now inserts it and tears down the composer **before** the GitHub round-trip, then swaps in the real comment on success or, on failure, removes the placeholder and reopens the composer with the draft restored. `submitReply` does the same for the inline reply box: it returns `true` immediately (so the box clears) and posts in the background, reopening a composer at the thread anchor if the post fails. `refreshPRComments` carries forward still-pending placeholders so a background refresh landing mid-post does not make them vanish.

callouts.body: Failure path: roll the placeholder back, reopen the composer at the same key, and restore the draft so the user can retry without retyping.
Guard against a refresh wiping an in-flight placeholder before its own create call reconciles it.

steps.title: No visible difference in the renderer
steps.body: `CommentAnnotation.svelte` is left untouched: an optimistic comment renders exactly like a posted one. The placeholder is built to be indistinguishable (viewer author and avatar, a `just now` timestamp, and the viewer's own edit/delete affordances via `canDelete: true`), so the user has no idea anything async is happening. The `optimistic` flag and negative id are internal bookkeeping only; nothing in the UI branches on them.
